Verified empirically with cobra v1.8.1 on Go 1.26.0 (`/tmp/cobra-demo`):

**Reproduction (bug path):**
```
Command order: [apple create zebra ]          # sorted alphabetically, not insertion order
bug: 'app apple --help' contains bug-flag?  false
bug: 'app zebra --help' contains bug-flag?  true   # flag landed on the WRONG command
fix: 'app create --help' contains name?     true    # variable-reference fix works
```

**Automated tests — 3 passed** (`go test -v ./...`):

| Test | Edge case covered | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `TestCommandsIndexIsSorted` | Confirms `Commands()[0]` is `alpha` when `zeta` was added first — index ≠ insertion order | PASS |
| `TestFixWorksRegardlessOfOrder` | Fix holds when subcommands are added in any order: `[create,zebra]`, `[zebra,create]`, `[apple,create,zebra]` | PASS |
| `TestFlagParseOnWrongCommand` | Runtime parse `app apple --bug-flag x` errors with unknown-flag because the flag leaked onto `zebra` — a silent misbehavior, not just a help-text nit | PASS |

Additional edge cases reasoned about: renaming a subcommand or inserting a new one before it would silently relocate flags under the index-based approach (no compile error, no runtime error — pure data corruption), whereas the variable-reference approach is immune because the reference never changes.
